[SCENE GEOMETRY & ARCHITECTURE]
Medium format architectural documentary photograph taken on a Mamiya 7 with a 45mm lens, f/8 aperture, fine-grain film. Elevated wide oblique perspective of the West End of Edinburgh looking north-east down Shandwick Place towards Charlotte Square.

In the mid-ground stands the monumental blonde Craigleith sandstone campanile and facade of St George’s West Church, featuring fine Roman Baroque detailing, giant pilasters, a rusticated ground level, clock faces, and an arched bell chamber topped with a weathered verdigris-green copper pyramidal roof. Flanking the broad roadway are unbroken, plumb Georgian and Victorian ashlar sandstone tenement terraces with channelled ground floors, classical cornices, sash windows, and pitched slate mansard roofs punctuated with stone chimney stacks and lead-clad dormers. In the far distance along the urban axis, the peristyle drum and pale green oxidized dome of West Register House punctuates the historic skyline. 

Sandstone surfaces exhibit fine tool marks, authentic rain-washed textures, and subtle historic carbon soot patinas in carved relief recesses. Dispersed mature European sycamores and elm trees display organic branching structures and leafy foliage rising from nearby gardens.
